items.title: Decide how a migrated keys::Action leaves the enum without bypassing the Typing guard (E-024 is blocked on this)
items.evidence: Decided by the developer 2026-10-22: actions name their operation. A keys::Action counts as migrated when its binding dispatches a registered operation, checked mechanically (the action names its operation id; the parity test verifies the id against the registry and that the UI path dispatches it). The Typing guard stays, because the action stays in keys::Action. The parity test's definition of 'migrated' changes accordingly, and the allowlist keeps shrinking: lower UNMIGRATED_MAX by one per migrated action. the_allowlist_of_unmigrated_actions_only_shrinks asserts UNMIGRATED.len() == Action::ALL.len() and that every variant is listed by name (operations_have_two_front_ends.rs ~400-421). Action is generated by enumerated! (keys.rs ~504-833), so a migrated action must be removed from the enum for the ratchet to shrink. Options: (a) bind the key straight from KeyboardInput in editor.rs, which must re-create the keys::Context Typing guard; (b) let keymap bindings name an operation so the enum keeps only human-only verbs. Option (b) is the design the parity rule implies. Needs a developer decision before E-024 can ship.

items.evidence: The stated symptom does not reproduce: with a hook that fires a chip's real `Activate`, the click writes the token to `project.measured` AND the clicked chip is the held one. items.title: Undoing a removal blanks the ground patches for one frame
items.evidence: Reproduced at 15 fps on the town map: the undo frame (f009, t=0.60 s) had 0 green field pixels where its neighbours have 143,694. Cause: a logged undo and an agent's undo ask for `Due::map_replaced`, whose `draw_every_placement` despawned EVERY standing piece before respawning the map. The person's Cmd+Z never blanked (143,694 across all 45 frames) because it takes the targeted path. Fixed: despawn only what the map no longer holds, and leave a piece alone only when it is drawn where its row says (position AND facing). Also: the put-back now spawns restored rows with their `Paint`. Test `a_full_redraw_leaves_the_standing_pieces_standing.rs` (first of two fails before).

items.title: A screenshot read back over BRP can be a stale file, and two reads can return the same bytes

must_fix.evidence: `bevy_debugger/screenshot` returns before the PNG lands; two captures taken 1.5 s apart came back with identical MD5 9702f3bd311ea207d07719077bf74572 in the E-048 iteration, which produced a 0-pixel 'no change' reading and a wrong diagnosis. Workaround: hash the path after a delay, or read the state instead.

items.evidence: `emerge_capture_still` returns a `fingerprint` (FNV-1a 64 hex) over the bytes it writes, so two stills compare as pictures; live: unchanged screen -> same value, after a camera move -> different. The raw `bevy_debugger/screenshot {path}` trap remains (it returns in 21 ms, the PNG lands ~200 ms later) and is now warned about in docs/guide/agents.md; our tools never hit it because `grab()` polls `bevy_debugger/capture` and writes the file itself. Also corrected `docs.rs`'s claim that it reads the server's source (TOOLS is a hand-kept copy; the drift ratchet caught this change).

items.title: A label receipt names the axis it set but not the effects a kind change re-settled

must_fix.evidence: `set_axis` re-settles implied effects when `kind` changes, so light -> decor drops `electricity`. The receipt says only `+decor -light`; the vocabulary decided the rest and the author is not told.

items.evidence: The receipt names the effects a `kind` write re-settled: `set kind on `town/brazier`  -light; effects  -emit`. Compared settled-to-settled, so a stale disk row cannot report a change the editor already showed (review gap G1). Two tests in `label_set_is_an_operation.rs`, both failing before the fix.

items.title: An `effects` write can be overridden by the vocabulary and the receipt does not say so

must_fix.evidence: `set_axis` settles `effects` after an effects write too, so an author removing an implied effect has it put back. The receipt reads `set effects on X  -inert` and never says `emit` stayed because the kind implies it. Found by E-063's review; same class as E-063 on the other axis.

items.evidence: An effects write that drops an implied token says so: `set effects on `town/brazier` — kept emit (the kind implies it)`. The kept tokens are read against the request, and the effects axis's 'as it was' is the SETTLED list — review found that reading the raw row reported the vocabulary's own effect as the author's addition (`+powered -inert`) on a file not yet caught up with its kind. 3 tests, the first and third failing before; live-verified on a scratch project with an implication.

items.title: A sequence that starts behind its own schedule finished before applying its operation
items.evidence: The mechanism is not the real-time deadline the item named. drive_sequencer's operation gate waits for `next >= 1`, so a run whose first tick is already past the last frame's time asks every frame with `next == 0` and finished with `operation_result: None`, after which the operation could never apply. The finish now also requires `!operation_pending`, and the next tick applies it. Mechanism corrected and recorded in the item because the wrong diagnosis is what let it stay open as 'flakiness'. crates/bevy_emerge_mapper/tests/a_sequence_started_behind_schedule_still_applies_its_operation.rs — failed before (operation_result null) on a dadb7ef worktree, passes after; the five existing sequencer tests are unchanged and pass in a full run.

must_fix.evidence: The gate stops meaning green: three consecutive `cargo test --workspace` runs at load 30-37 each failed a different sequencer test, so no iteration's evidence could be trusted.

items.title: The file watcher overwrote unsaved edits: it compared the file with the in-memory map

must_fix.evidence: watch::adopt_map compared the re-read file with `open.map`, the map that HOLDS unsaved edits, so any save from anywhere followed by an unsaved edit inside the 250 ms poll replaced the edit with the file. Silent: the map on screen and the map on disk then agree, so nothing looks wrong. This is the real cause of the intermittent a_person_removes_a_piece_and_undoes_it::an_agents_undo_of_a_removal_waits_while_the_person_has_moved_a_piece_since failure, which was reported as flakiness.

items.evidence: Adoption now compares against what was last saved or read (OpenMap::saved()), refuses with `changed on disk while this map has unsaved edits` when the person has unsaved work, and only then takes the file. crates/bevy_emerge_mapper/tests/an_unsaved_edit_survives_the_watcher.rs (2 tests, both failing before).

items.title: No operation opens a map by name, so an agent that made a map cannot work in it

must_fix.evidence: accept.py step 3: `map_create` makes `courtyard` and then the agent has no way in. `door_open` selects a door and a tab, and its parameters are door and tab only. The script's workaround is to relaunch the editor on the map, which an agent cannot do to a person's session.

items.evidence: `map_open` reads the file through `OpenMap::open` (the Map tab's own door) and asks the editor to cross to the Map door through the same `DoorRequest` path `door_open` uses; `screen::cross` now dispatches it too, so a person crossing and an agent opening are one operation. A map that does not exist is refused rather than started — the one place it differs from `+ new map`. accept.py step `open_map`: fail -> pass. One limit recorded as E-078: from the menu the editor cannot be entered, so the script's relaunch workaround stays.

items.title: A BRP call that takes longer than 5 s is reported as "is the editor running?"

must_fix.evidence: Measured 2026-10-25 at load average 32: `emerge/operation_apply` for `map_create` on Sanctuary's project exceeded the server's 5 s global BRP timeout and the answer read `the editor did not answer `emerge/operation_apply` ... Is it running, and is BEVY_BRP_PORT the same on both sides?` while the editor was up and answered `emerge/project_root` 6.7 s after launch. The timeout is in bevy_emerge_mcp/src/brp.rs (`timeout_global(5 s)`) and it is a considered choice — a tool call an agent waits on should not hang — but the refusal's words blame the wrong thing, and an operation that parses a project (or a fill that lays 4096 cells, or a capture's landing wait) legitimately takes longer.

items.evidence: crates/bevy_emerge_mcp/src/brp.rs (MUTATING_TIMEOUT, cec92c1); tests brp::tests::a_slow_editor_is_not_blamed_on_the_connection, a_missing_editor_is_named_as_missing

items.title: An agent cannot enter the editor: an operation cannot move the screen, so a map made from the menu cannot be worked in without a relaunch

must_fix.evidence: Measured 2026-10-25 with the S1 live proof: `map_create` then `map_open` both apply from the menu, and the editor stays on the menu — a 3 s capture sequence taken afterwards shows the MAPS column, not the viewport. `apply_pending_door` runs `in_state(Screen::Editor)` and `EditorState` does not exist on the menu, so the door-request mechanism cannot cross an editor boundary; the menu enters the editor through `Chooser::open_the_selection` -> `launch_args` -> `NextState`, which is the screen's, not an operation's. `tools/loop/accept.py` works around it by relaunching the editor on the map, and records the workaround.
